The Low Countries [ a ] is a historical and geographically coastal lowland region in Northwestern Europe forming the lower basin of the Rhine–Meuse–Scheldt delta and consisting today of the three modern " Benelux " countries: Belgium , the Netherlands , and Luxembourg . Also sometimes included are parts of France (such as Nord and Pas-de-Calais ) and the German regions of East Frisia , Guelders and Cleves . Since the creation of the Holy Roman Empire , the region has been divided into numerous different entities. [ 1 ] [ 2 ]
